full_judgment:
6. The Family Court decreed the suit in part declaring that the plaintiff is entitled to take the twin sons in her custody holding that the defendant did not allow the plaintiff to see the twin sons on 30.9.93 which has been supported by P.Ws. 1 an 2. The defendant preferred Family Appeal No. 10 of 1995 which was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, who by judgment and decree dated 5.8.95 allowed the appeal. The plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No. 3692 of 1995 before this court against the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below and this Court by judgment and order dated 10.12.97 made the Rule absolute restoring the judgment of the trial court. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the defendant-petitioner preferred civil Petition No. 306 of 1998 before the Hon'ble Appellate Division id the leave petition was summarily rejected on 5.5.98. 

 7. Pursuant thereto the decree holder opposite party put the decree into execution in Family Court Execution Case No. 7 of 1998 before the learned Assistant Judge, 6th Court Dhaka. The petitioner filed an application before the executing court for keeping the twin sons in his custody till December, 1998 on the ground that the minor sons are carrying on studies in the Fulpur kindergarten, Mymensingh and they would complete their annual examination in December 1996. The learned executing court kept the application for hearing. The petitioner also filed an application for directing the decree-holder opposite party to supply him the particulars of her present address on the ground that he visited the address of 88, Rayer Bazar where the owner of the house Mr. E.R. Hossain Dewan told him that the plaintiff left the house in 1996 and married for the second time and on enquiry the petitioner learnt that the plaintiff in fact married for the second time and thereafter she is not legally entitled to the custody of the minors under section 352 and 354 of the Muslim Law. The application was filed supported by affidavit with a copy to the plaintiff opposite party but she did not file any counter-affidavit disputing the positive statements made therein. The learned Executing Court by order dated 21.7.98 rejected the application on the ground that the Executing Court cannot go behind the decree. 

 9. The opposite party by filing counter affidavit dated 22.11.98 denied the material allegations made in the revisional application and further asserted that the petitioners application before the learned Executing Court was totally misconceived, misleading and not maintainable and it was filed only to delay the execution of the decree which she obtained up to the Appellate Division and therefore the learned Executing Court rightly rejected the same by the impugned judgment and order. It was further contended that the petitioner filed the application before the Executing Court on 20.7.98 and the learned Advocate for the opposite party received the copy on the same date raising serious objection and showing the necessity of submitting written objection upon the same. The learned Court heard the zip: plication on the self-same date. Therefore, there was no scone of submitting counter affidavit upon the same. On 27.8.98 the decree holder filed an application before the Executing Court supplying her new address of Room No. 210. IIishium Bhaban. Tikatuli, Dhaka where she has been residing since 13.7.96 after getting allotment from Government. It was further asserted that the plaintiff opposite party has never married for the second time. Mr. Daud Khan of Police Station Singair, District Manikganj is not known to her. She had never gone to Shikaripara, Nowabganj and never signed any kabinnama. The so-called kabinnama which has been produced before this Court is a forged one and the petitioner created the same with the help of his men only to create a new story and to make delay in handing over the minors to the mother. By further affidavit dated 7.12.8 the plaintiff opposite party asserted that she filed a petition of complaint being C.R. Case No. 201 of 1998 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class, Nawabganj against the creator, of the forged kabinnama for taking legal action against them. The learned Magistrate took cognizance of the case on 26.11.98 and issued summons. 

 13. Therefore, the vital point for consideration in this case is whether the plaintiff opposite, party got married for the second time. It may be stated here that the plaintiff's suit was decreed upto the Appellate Division observing that the plaintiff was entitled to take the twin sons in her custody. It is on record that the plaintiff and defendant are highly educated persons and they are responsible Government Officers. The plaintiff has been working as Assistant Secretary under the Government and the defendant petitioner is a Thana Nirbahi Officer, posted at Fulpur, District Mymensingh at present. From the judgment of the Appellate 'Division, it appears that the defendant-petitioner has got married again and as such the welfare of the twin sons will not be protected in the hands of the step-mother. Mr. Khan further submits that the so-called marriage as per kabinnama filed by the petitioner took place on 17.12.96 and the judgment of the Appellate Division was delivered on 28.5.98 and during this long period the petitioner did not bring this important fact of so-called 2nd marriage of the plaintiff opposite party to the notice of the Court. He also submits that this goes to support the contention of the plaintiff-opposite party that the so-called kabinnama was created for the purpose of delaying the disposal' of the execution case pending before the Executing Court.
